relevance_note: Single case report of a man diagnosed with Alexander disease: "An elderly man over 70 years old with Alexander's disease (AD)"; no GFAP variant or genetic test is reported.
method_note: Written by hand with a short Python script that resolved each quote to the exact paper text (thin spaces U+2009, hyphens U+2010, en dashes) and verified every span verbatim. One in-scope person (label 'patient', rule 5). No GFAP variant, genetic testing or parental testing is reported; the Discussion mentions GFAP only in general, so the variants table is empty and clinical_diagnosis_basis is 'not reported' (the paper says only 'had been diagnosed with AD'). n_patients_reported is null because the paper describes no patient with a GFAP variant (one patient with a diagnosis of Alexander disease). Age: the abstract says 'A 70-year-old man' and the case presentation 'An elderly man over 70 years old'; recorded 70-year-old as age at last evaluation, though it is the age at presentation and he died about 1 year after the second drainage (age at death not stated, so deceased_age is null). Age at diagnosis is not stated (diagnosed '9 years ago', not converted). Onset recorded as 'Adult-onset' with no ISO value; feature onsets '9 years ago', '2 weeks prior' and '4 months after drainage' are times relative to presentation, so onset_iso8601 is null. The Discussion's general statement that pyramidal lesions, cerebellar ataxia, dysuria and sleep problems are prevalent in adult-onset AD is not about this patient and was not used. 'Loss of motor control' was not mapped to limb weakness. No brain imaging is reported; all MRI checklist items are not reported. Bladder stones and hydronephrosis were not mapped to autonomic (bladder) dysfunction. Minor inconsistency: fever 38–39°C in the abstract vs 37.9°C on examination; both kept as detail.
